$comment: The data domains starter tree (data taxonomy, D-37; docs/architecture/data-taxonomy.md): six domains at level domain, fifteen subdomains at level subdomain, flat rows with a parent key (V03).

Every top-level domain sets a classification (V52). A subdomain with no classification inherits the one above it; the subdomains that hold personal, contract or pay data are classified restricted, higher than their domain, never lower (V53).
No handling rule is set on a domain, so each follows its classification's defaults. An install tightens a branch, such as AI use of payroll set to never, through a configuration change.
Examples tell an AI client what belongs in each domain, so it can suggest mappings. They are untrusted text.

values.label: Customers
values.examples: Who the customers are and how the business serves them: accounts, contacts, cases.

values.label: Client accounts
values.examples: Customer organizations, their addresses, segments and account managers.

values.label: Client contacts
values.examples: Named people at customers: names, emails, phone numbers and their roles.

values.label: Service cases
values.examples: Customer questions, complaints and support cases with their history.

values.label: Commercial
values.examples: How the business sells: proposals, contracts and orders.

values.label: Proposals
values.examples: Quotes, bids and opportunities with their prices and status.

values.label: Contracts
values.examples: Signed agreements with customers and suppliers, their terms and prices.

values.label: Client orders
values.examples: Orders, order lines, delivery dates and order status.

values.label: People
values.examples: Everything about the people who work for the business.

values.label: Personnel records
values.examples: Employee files: contracts of employment, job history, reviews and absence.

values.label: Payroll
values.examples: Salary, deductions, tax codes and bank details for pay.

values.label: Timesheets
values.examples: Hours worked per person, project and day, with approvals.

values.label: Operations
values.examples: How the business delivers its work in the field and in its sites.

values.label: Field operations
values.examples: Work orders, visits, inspections and findings in the field.

values.label: Warehouse
values.examples: Stock levels, parts, locations and movements of goods.

values.label: Finance
values.examples: The money of the business: ledgers, invoices and payments.

values.label: General ledger
values.examples: Accounts, journals, cost centers and period closes.

values.label: Supplier invoices
values.examples: Invoices from suppliers, their approvals and payment status.

values.label: Workplace
values.examples: The places people work and the services there.

values.label: Facilities
values.examples: Buildings, floors, maintenance requests and contractors on site.

values.label: Room bookings
values.examples: Meeting room and desk reservations.
